messages:
Maya (PM): heads up — saw an uptick in error reports for the streaming fallback path after launch. customer impact looks like missing tokens in ~2% of sessions. tagging this for a quick triage: bug vs enhancement?
Olivia (CS): getting a couple of escalations from big-account support. they hit it in >50% of sessions when using long-context prompts. they want a reliability fix asap.
Eric (Eng): can you paste an example stack/req? suspect KV cache invalidation around rollover.
Olivia (CS): example pasted in thread: session id 9f8a3, 2nd chunk dropped, user saw truncated output. repro steps in their report: 1) send 2.5k token prompt 2) call streaming endpoint 3) send followup -> truncated.
Sam (SWE): ok I can reproduce locally with the long prompt. quick log: `kv_cache_miss at seq 1024` then `stream_flush` before tokens sent.
Maya (PM): options: (A) emergency patch to ensure flush ordering (est 1 dev-day + canary), (B) workaround in SDK to throttle chunking (client-side, ~half day), (C) treat as enhancement and schedule next sprint. need decision on scope and launch criteria for the fix.
Liz (Design): any UX regressions from workaround? throttling might make streaming feel choppier for small prompts.
Sam (SWE): workaround reduces throughput for a subset; fixes truncation but increases latency for some flows.
Eric (Eng): technical tradeoff: patch is straightforward but touches runtime flush order — needs careful rollout + e2e. I'd estimate 1.5 dev-days incl. tests + 2h canary + rollback plan.
Maya (PM): severity: Olivia says major accounts affected, potential churn risk. propose: ship patch now as P0, SDK workaround as short-term mitigation while we land tests. allocated squad for today?
Olivia (CS): customer asks for ETA today — please prioritize.
Sam (SWE): I can pick up the patch today, will open PR with `fix/stream-flush-order`. planning to include a unit test reproducing the seq boundary and an integration test against streaming harness.
Eric (Eng): I'll pair on canary and validation; will prepare a tiny perf test to verify no perf regression <2%.
Maya (PM): acceptance criteria for this hotfix: 1) repro no longer occurs in staging with long-context harness, 2) production canary (5% traffic) for 1 hour with no truncation reports, 3) rollback plan documented and exercised. if all green, promote to 100% after 3h.
Sam (SWE): noted. I'll add a short runbook: `if truncation_rate > 0.1% during canary -> rollback`.
Liz (Design): we'll prepare a short customer-facing note explaining the fix and expected behavior change.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: `fix/stream-flush-order` -> staging at 2765432133
Sam (SWE): PR opened: https://git.internal/r/1234, tests attached. starting staging run now.
Eric (Eng): staging looks clean so far, running long-run harness. will stand by for canary window.
Maya (PM): decision check: we prioritize bug patch now. enhancement to improve streaming UX (adaptive chunking) moves to next sprint backlog. any objections?
Liz (Design): agree.
Olivia (CS): thanks, please ping when canary starts.
Sam (SWE): canary started at 2765432160 on 5% traffic. monitoring dashboards pinned to channel.
Maya (PM): great — tagging follow-up milestone: `postlaunch-iteration/streaming-reliability` for the enhancement after hotfix. owner: Liz + Sam.
Eric (Eng): if canary stays green for 1h we'll roll to 100% and close the incident. I'll post a short postmortem draft after.
Maya (PM): thanks team. will update stakeholders and add acceptance criteria to the ticket.
Olivia (CS): customer update sent.
deploy-bot: deploy promoted to 100% at 2765432225 (auto-rollout)
Sam (SWE): monitoring shows 0 truncation reports in 3h window, closing thread.
Maya (PM): closing notes: hotfix shipped, enhancement scheduled for next sprint, action item owners: Sam (patch), Eric (canary+postmortem), Liz (customer note + follow-on spec), Olivia (customer comms).
